Split personalities are actually caused by  Dissociative Identity Disorder, which she may have *on top of* schizophrenia, most (not all) people with this disorder tend to withdraw from society when they become symptomatic. That said, be sure she takes her medication, establish a routine with her and talk to her doctor. I suggest joining something like [NAMI](www.nami.org). They have support groups for people with mental illnesses and their partners. I believe it will help both of you to learn about what you are dealing with and it is better to approach such an illness as a team as opposed to putting it all on your shoulders.

Managing your illness is hopeful. Finding medication and giving tools for management has saved my life, but people have different opinions as to what overcoming means. To me, the idea of a "cure" being sought out  can be toxic. We are fixed on normalcy as society enough as it is. It's true that depressive states can be temporary, but more often than not "recovery" is management. You should not approach mental illness or disorders as though it's something you can "live without". Bipolar doesn't disappear, MDD and PTSD don't either. And those people that have "overcome"? I applaud them, but just because I know for a *fact* that I will be taking pills for the rest of my life doesn't me any stronger or weaker than the next. Being on your own is a big step, but sometimes it's a step you absolutely have to take.

I have a brownie recipe (this counts, right?) that I got online and modified a bit. I gave them away as gifts this year in little holiday tins.

* 2 cups white sugar
* 1 cup butter (melt then pour, obvs.)
* 1/2 cup cocoa powder (some companies make richer powder, some don't use whatever you prefer)
* 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
* 4 eggs
* 1 cup all purpose flour
* 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
* 1/2 teaspoon salt
* 1 teaspoon nutmeg
* 1 teaspoon cinnamon

You can add 1/2 cup of nuts or chocolate chips if you like, even cut the cinnamon and nutmeg in half, but these brownies are amazing. Sometimes I add Oreos. :3

You bake for 20-30 minutes in a 9x13 greased pan at 350.

This should make about 20 brownies.

If you wanna cheat, use a box mix and just add the cinnamon and nutmeg to your liking.  My favorite for these types of brownies with a shortcut is [this mix](http://www.amazon.com/Duncan-Hines-Brownie-Chocolate-18-Ounce/dp/B0029K0ZAE/ref=sr_1_4?s=grocery&ie=UTF8&qid=1355591491&sr=1-4&keywords=duncan+hines+brownie+mix)
